pageCache.pageTitle: Stonar School | Independent School in Wiltshire
pageCache.text:
Home
Established in 1895, Stonar is a co-educational day and boarding school for pupils aged 2-18, nestled in the stunning Wiltshire countryside. We offer a nurturing approach and a broad, balanced curriculum, enabling them to achieve academically and pastorally.
Welcoming riders of all abilities, Stonar is widely regarded as the UK's leading equestrian school.
Welcoming children from age 2-4 years old, specialist teachers build pupils' knowledge and skills through learning and play.
Lessons are based on thematic units and we emphasise creativity, sport and outdoor education. Pupils are nurtured to shine academically and personally.
Consistently in the top 10% of schools nationally for value-added at GCSE, Senior pupils not only enjoy a broad, progressive curriculum and excellent pastoral care, they also achieve highly.
Individual mentoring, small class sizes and a wealth of co curricular and leadership opportunities help students prepare for life beyond Stonar.
Three boarding houses nestled in our 80 acre countryside grounds provide an idyllic setting for pupils to thrive in our kind, familial environment.
An independent day and boarding school with global goals, Stonar pupils achieve highly and thrive as individuals. Our impressive teaching team develop supportive relationships with our pupils, providing both challenge and support to ensure pupils make the most of every opportunity available to them.
We set high standards for our pupils and are proud of exceptional achievement across the school. Our learners are afforded a high degree of personalised attention in a supportive yet challenging educational environment.
Stonar has a unique charm and a calm contentedness. The School prides itself on having a community built on kindness and integrity; pupils here are heard and supported, and their self-confidence flourishes.
Sport, riding, drama, public speaking, music, art, photography, languages, outdoor expeditions, leadership …we expect our pupils to get involved in all aspects of a rich and varied school life.
A countryside school with global goals. Stonar pupils are fortunate to be part of a forward-thinking international group of schools.
Stonar Prep was delighted to welcome back former pupil Emmy K, who returned to the school to unveil a brand-new Friendship Bench.
Explore the Senior School and Sixth Form Centre, meeting teachers, pupils and hearing from the Headmaster to discover more about life at Stonar.
Mr Cunningham, Head of Prep, explores the tradition of the Harvest Festival
A warm, welcoming boarding community where pupils of all ages live together harmoniously and build friendships for life.
Catering for complete beginners to experienced, competitive riders. World-class equestrian centre on-site.
Explore our 90-acre countryside campus.

Our Mission
At Stonar, our mission is to prepare each pupil to thrive in a globalised world by supporting them to develop the skills, knowledge and self-assurance to succeed academically and personally.
The quality of pupils' academic and other achievements is excellent."
ISI Inspection Report
WORK HARD
We set high standards for our pupils and are proud of exceptional achievement across the school. Our learners are afforded a high degree of personalised attention in a supportive yet challenging educational environment. The result is that Stonar is consistently listed in the top 10% of schools for value-added, meaning that pupils regularly obtain higher results than predicted. In the Prep School, we offer an innovative enquiry led Primary Curriculum, which emphasises creativity, sport and outdoor education, combined with developing an international-mindedness through engaging thematic units.. Thematic learning continues for pupils in Years 7 and 8, as pupils work towards the Stonar Diploma. As our Senior pupils enter their exam years, they have the opportunity to choose from a broad range of subjects for GCSE, A Level and Diploma courses. Each year approximately 95% of our students gain entrance to their chosen university.
BE KIND
We are a community of over 440 pupils and over 60 teachers. Our pupils are treated as individuals, so whether they are 2 or 18, they are well-known by their teachers, form tutors, house parents and peers across the school.
Stonar has a unique charm and a calm contentedness. The school prides itself on having a community built on kindness and integrity; pupils here are heard and supported, and their self-confidence flourishes.
Pupils have the freedom to be themselves without fear of being judged. Children enjoy a joyful education because they are not pressured to conform, but rather encouraged to explore, blossom and discover their true passions.
GET INVOLVED
Sport, riding, drama, public speaking, music, art, photography, languages, outdoor expeditions, leadership… we expect our pupils to get involved in all aspects of a rich and varied school life.
For riders, Stonar’s offer is remarkable; we are home to the UK’s finest riding academy and the immersive experience here produces highly successful equestrian teams. Pupils may bring their own horse to school or loan one of the Stonar stable. The facilities are at the heart of the School, and highly qualified staff support learners to achieve dedicated equestrian qualifications (BHS and BTEC).
Around 40% of pupils ride, including over half of our boarding community, but many more non-riders enjoy coming to the stables and patting their favourite ponies at break or lunchtime.
With a large, open, rural site of 90 acres and stunning views of the Wiltshire countryside, our pupils enjoy making the most of being outdoors - be that for sports lessons, lunch time play or after school activities.
SHAPE THE WORLD
A countryside school with global goals. Stonar pupils are fortunate to be part of a forward-thinking international group of schools.
We ensure opportunities to develop a global outlook through the school’s cohort, curriculum and trips. There are plentiful learning opportunities through partnerships with organisations such as WWF and LEGO - and collaborative projects with pupils in partner schools. As a member of the Globeducate group, Stonar prides itself on developing individuals with a global mindset.
We ensure that our pupils build character, learn skills and develop abilities beyond the purely academic.
Our young people have a voice. Our pupils have the power to act and help build a more equal, fair and sustainable society. We prepare each of our pupils to become a global citizen who can shape the world.
We wanted an environment that let children discover their strengths and areas that interested them...Stonar is that school."
Stonar At A Glance
'Excellent' - ISI Rating
Day and Boarding, 130 full boarders
Impressive value added at GCSE and A Level results
Welcoming 440 pupils from over 15 different countries, 80% British pupils
Outstanding pastoral care tailored to the individual
Academically ambitious for all pupils
World-class onsite equestrian provision
A broad and progressive curriculum
Many schools talk about treating the child as an individual, but Stonar actually does it!"
Stonar School is an independent day and boarding school set on a 90-acre rural campus in Wiltshire, established in 1895. The school welcomes around 440 pupils from over 15 countries and combines strong academic standards with extensive outdoor and equestrian facilities.
Stonar School educates children from early years through to 18, with day and boarding options available. Boarding is offered from age 9 upwards, with approximately 130 full boarders and a supportive residential community.
Stonar School is renowned for its world-class onsite equestrian provision, often described as the UK’s finest riding academy. Pupils can bring or loan horses, and receive expert coaching aimed at BHS and BTEC equestrian qualifications. Around 40% of pupils ride, including over half of the boarding community.
Stonar School delivers an enquiry-led Primary Curriculum in the Prep School, thematic learning for Years 7–8 (Stonar Diploma), and a broad choice of GCSE, A Level and Diploma courses in the Senior School. The school consistently ranks in the top 10% for value‑added and achieves excellent ISI inspection outcomes, with around 95% of pupils progressing to their chosen university.
Stonar School emphasises outstanding, individualised pastoral care within a close-knit community of teachers and house staff. Pupils are encouraged to take part in sport, drama, music, public speaking, outdoor expeditions and leadership opportunities, and benefit from international partnerships (including WWF and LEGO) that foster a global mindset.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headmaster | Stonar School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headmaster
It is a great privilege to be Headmaster of Stonar, and particularly special now that my three children are Stonarians too.
Like any parent, I want my children to be happy at school. I want them to be known and cared for, to have great friends and wonderful experiences, and to look forward to coming to learn each morning. I also want them to be challenged however. I want them to work hard, discover what they are capable of, develop resilience and leave school prepared as well as excited about whatever comes next.
I don't think, as parents, we should have to choose between challenge and happiness.
At Stonar, we capture this belief in three simple words: Achieve with joy.
We are ambitious for our pupils, and achievement matters to us. Of course, that includes academic results, but it means much more besides. Success is different for every young person. It might be outstanding examination results, a performance on stage, success on the sports field or in equestrian, mastering a new skill or overcoming something that once seemed impossible. Sometimes, achievement begins simply with finding the confidence to have a go and explore their potential.
Nobody achieves entirely on their own. Young people need to be known, encouraged and supported by people who believe in what they can become. This is why the concept of Stonar educators is so important to me. Our teachers are educators, but so too are the many people across Stonar who coach, mentor, listen, care and create opportunities for our pupils every day. Whatever our role in the School, we all play a part in helping young people to grow, fulfil their potential and become the best version of themselves.
In more than 25 years in education, I have seen first-hand that young people achieve more when they feel secure in themselves, know that they are valued and enjoy school life. Joy is not about making life easy or avoiding difficulties. Young people need to be challenged and inspired. They need to learn from mistakes, develop resilience and understand that worthwhile achievements usually require effort and perseverance. We are, after all, preparing them not simply for the next stage of their education, but for life beyond Stonar.
Parents are an important part of that journey too. I have always believed that the best education comes through genuine partnership between school and home. As young people grow, they must also take increasing responsibility for their choices, their contribution to the community and the person they want to become. Education is ultimately something we do together, but its purpose is to give young people the confidence and independence to make their own way in life.
Our values express that purpose rather well: Work hard. Be kind. Get involved. Shape the world.
They are deliberately straightforward, but they are also demanding. We want Stonarians to make the most of their abilities and understand the value of effort; to be thoughtful and compassionate in the way they treat others; and to get involved, because some of the most important learning happens when we step forward, participate and try something new. Ultimately, we want them to leave Stonar ready to shape their own lives and make a positive difference in the lives of others.
That, to me, is lifelong learning. It is also what it means to Achieve with joy.
Of course, you cannot understand a school fully from a website. You need to walk around it, meet our people and, most importantly, talk to our pupils. I hope you will come and visit us, experience Stonar for yourself and discover a school that is warm and caring, but also energetic, ambitious and full of opportunity.
I very much look forward to welcoming you.
Aaron J. G. King Headmaster
Our approach is summed up in three words: “Achieve with joy.” We believe joy - a deep sense of self-worth and security - drives curiosity, resilience and lasting achievement. Pupils are encouraged to excel academically while being supported emotionally so they become well‑rounded, confident individuals.
Stonar offers both boarding and day provision within a kind, calm, family‑orientated environment. Pastoral care is central: pupils are known, supported and encouraged so achievement does not come at the expense of wellbeing. For current availability and boarding options, please contact Admissions.
You are welcome to visit the campus to experience Stonar first‑hand. We also offer a virtual tour of our 90‑acre rural site and publish a weekly newsletter, Stonar Matters, which prospective parents can read for news and insight. Contact Admissions via the website to arrange a visit or request further information.

MUSIC
Music is at the heart of life in the Prep School, with children enjoying instrumental and vocal tuition with a specialist Music teacher as part of the curriculum both in class and in our specialist Music building.
We encourage every child to play and perform in assemblies and class, as well as at formal and informal concerts. Music is very popular and many children take music exams.
DRAMA
Drama helps to build a child’s confidence, creativity and communication skills. The Prep children love performing and there are plenty of opportunities for them to try out a variety of styles in weekly lessons with specialist Drama teachers. Many will take part in productions, festivals and public events, performing to varied audiences.
A specialist drama teacher also coaches those from Year 2 upwards who are keen to take LAMDA (London Academy of Music and Dramatic Arts) qualifications.

pageCache.text:
Directors And Advisory Board
Stonar is part of the international private school group (Globeducate Schools Group) with headquarters in Spain. The School is governed by a Board of Directors that sets and reviews the policies, plans and procedures that will ensure the best possible education for present and future pupils, including the proper control of its finances.
The Directors' duties are to protect the assets of the School and to ensure that it is diligently and well run. The Chair of the Board of Directors is Mr Daniel Jones.
Directors are expected to exercise independent judgement with reasonable care and diligence. They have to act fairly and in a manner that protects the reputation of the School.
It is their duty to keep in mind the interests of pupils, staff and parents, as well as that of the community.
They ensure that the School complies with the law, is solvent and complies with the financial regulations. It must be adequately insured against possible public and employers’ liability (including Directors’ liability) claims. The Directors must declare any personal interest in any transaction or arrangement proposed by the School, to avoid conflicts of interest and not to accept benefits from interested third parties.
Chief Education Officer
Chief Operating Officer & Chief Marketing Officer
Mr Daniel Jones c/o Director of Finance and HR Stonar Cottles Park Atworth Melksham SN12 8NT
Reports at twice-yearly Advisory Board meetings provide the members and Directors with detailed information about the School’s successes and challenges for the future. The Head’s report includes summaries from various subject departments, which give the members and Directors a clear view of the School’s academic provision. Heads of Departments meet regularly with the Advisory Board member responsible for Educational Delivery within the Globeducate group of schools and present on their subject area or aspect of school life. This visit includes observing lessons. At board meetings, Directors debate all aspects of school life carefully and participate in relevant training. Safeguarding and welfare, health and safety are given particular emphasis at board meetings. The Directors have specific responsibility for reviewing Stonar’s safeguarding policy annually and for maintaining a suitable accessibility plan for those pupils with special educational needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our History: Over a Century of Excellence | Stonar School
pageCache.text:
History of Stonar School
Stonar, now 130 years old, was originally established at Stour House in Sandwich and can be traced back as far as 1895.
In 1920, Stour House School was taken over by three joint heads: Miss Gladys Crook, Miss Isabel Blackwell and Miss Edith Joslin, affectionately known as "the Three". They were pioneering educators with a progressive outlook and they expanded the school to the extent that it outgrew its premises. Everything was packed up and moved over the bridge to Stonar House to be "close to the sea, smoke-free air and spacious accommodation." From then on it became Stonar House School.
With its newly acquired extensive grounds, the first Stonar pony arrived – Tufty. By 1934 riding was firmly established at Stonar House.
Stonar House remained the school's home until 1939 and the outbreak of the Second World War, when the MOD requisitioned the land and the entire school community was forced to decamp. Luckily, one of the Heads had relatives in Wiltshire who alerted her to Cottles Park. The school was packed up again and moved to its current location. The school ponies, a goat called Ambrosia, a dog, a cat and a bowl of goldfish moved too.
We were a tired and almost exhausted group of Stonarites who arrived late evening at our new domicile – Cottles Park – was it to be worth it in the future? The present Stonar School, Cottles Park must be the answer."
The 'Three' continued to run Stonar until they retired in the 1960s. They valued equality of opportunity and offered a diverse range of subjects. They also placed great emphasis on outdoor education and personalised attention for each pupil. Their successor Miss Doreen Denmark expanded and developed the school for 20 years, until her retirement in the 1980s.
Since then, Stonar and its unique Equestrian Centre have flourished, with a committed staff, strong governance and excellent facilities within its superb parkland setting.
Founded as a single-sex independent, non-denominational school, we decided to accept boys throughout the Prep School. Following this successful transition, 2016 was our first year of Senior co-education and the school is now fully co-educational.
Stonar was acquired by the Globeducate Group in 2013, a leading international schools group that is committed to developing and enhancing the educational provision at Stonar, while ensuring it continues to retain what makes it special. Crucially, the school's pervading ethos from its earliest days, of warmth, support, a 'can-do' attitude and a pioneering spirit are as strong as ever!

pageCache.pageTitle: ISI Inspection Reports & School Reviews | Stonar School
pageCache.text:
ISI Inspection Report and Reviews
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) described Stonar as ‘Excellent’ - the highest possible rating - in an inspection report published in October 2018, which praises pupils’ excellent academic progress and outstanding social development.
The three-day inspection took place in October 2018 and focused on two key outcomes: academic achievement and personal development. Inspectors observed every aspect of school life including lessons, assemblies, tutorial sessions, boarding and extracurricular activities. They also conducted formal interviews with pupils and met staff from across the school. The key findings of the report, listed below, speak for themselves and are a fantastic testimonial to the high-calibre teaching and support that pupils receive.

Pupils of all ages have excellent attitudes to learning and are hard-working, positive and resilient learners.
Pupils achieve very well academically across all curriculum areas.
Pupils with SEND and/or EAL achieve highly as a result of the support that they receive.
Pupils make excellent progress, enabled by teaching that treats them as individuals.
Pupils are confident, highly considerate and respectful towards others.
Pupils have a naturally collaborative approach that benefits their ability to develop problem- solving skills.
Pupils’ social development is outstanding, enhanced by their excellent relationships with teachers.
It is clear from reading the report that Stonar offers pupils of all ages a superb educational experience. We are absolutely delighted to have received such a tremendous endorsement of the work of Stonar. I would like to thank all our staff, pupils and parents for their contributions to the success of the school.
Former Head, Dr Sally Divall commented at the time.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery Curriculum and Admissions | Stonar School
pageCache.text:
What We Offer
A Nurturing Environment Children thrive when they feel safe and supported. Our staff build warm relationships with every child and ensure their individual needs are understood and met.
Learning Through Play We follow the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, which supports children’s learning and development through a wide range of experiences across seven key areas.
Activities are carefully planned to encourage exploration, creativity, and independence for children 2 years and above.
Skilled & Caring Practitioners Our team is dedicated, experienced, and passionate about early education. We observe, listen, and guide - ensuring your child progresses at their own pace while feeling happy and secure.
Communication With Families We value open and honest communication. You’ll receive regular updates about your child’s achievements, interests, and next steps, helping you feel connected to their learning journey.
Inclusive Practice We celebrate diversity and welcome families from all backgrounds. Every child is unique, and we tailor our support to ensure everyone has the opportunity to flourish.
Every Monday and Friday, our Early Years children enjoy swimming sessions led by our specialist PE teachers. Lessons take place in small groups, allowing each child to feel supported, safe, and confident in the water. Through gentle guidance and playful activities, children begin to develop early swimming skills while having fun and building independence.
On Mondays and Fridays, children enjoy lively Spanish sessions led by our Senior School language teachers through songs, play, and simple activities, they are introduced to colours, numbers, and everyday vocabulary. These early experiences help build confidence, curiosity, and a love of language from the very start.
Our children enjoy a visit to our onsite Equestrian Centre to pat a pony every other week! This gentle, hands-on experience introduces children to the basics of caring for ponies in a safe, nurturing environment. With guidance from experienced staff, the children learn how to look after the ponies, develop confidence around animals, and practise brushing their soft fur. It’s a wonderful way to encourage empathy, responsibility, and a love of nature.
Sessions are carefully planned to be inclusive, engaging, and tailored to the age and abilities of each child. Whether it is acting out a favourite tale, inventing their own characters, or using movement and expression to tell a story without words, our young learners are encouraged to explore, experiment, and enjoy the magic of drama.
Children take part in our much-loved outdoor adventure sessions. We enjoy a short walk to our woodland area, where the children have the opportunity to explore, discover and learn in a natural environment.
During our adventure sessions, children can climb small trees and stumps, developing their confidence, coordination and problem-solving skills. Here there is a sense of freedom within safe parameters. We often get creative; one of our favourite activities is making forest friends using mud, clay and natural materials found in the woods.
Our children love being active! Each week, they enjoy sessions in our Sports Hall or out on the field, where they develop essential ball skills such as throwing, kicking, and catching. Sports gives children the chance to have fun, build confidence, and learn new skills.
Through hands-on exploration of instruments such as drums and shakers, children discover how different sounds are created and experiment freely with making their own music. Activities that involve recognising and following simple tunes help to build focus, auditory memory, and early musical awareness. Singing remains a joyful and integral part of our day, supporting children’s language development, confidence, and sense of belonging. Music also becomes a powerful storytelling tool, enabling children to interpret narratives, express emotions and bring stories to life through sound and movement.
Stonar is such a wonderful school and has been such a superb place for our son. He has greatly grown in confidence and his learning has really developed since joining the Nursery. Thank you for all the care and attention shown to him since joining in September. It truly has been a wonderful start to his education. We couldn't have wished for better."

Wraparound Care
The morning care and after-lesson experience is a cosy, homely environment, to support the needs of working parents and families with children in the Senior School. Pupils enjoy afternoon tea, and extending their day with their peers.
Known as 'Before and After School Club', our flexible wraparound provision is included within the school fees (*) and offers an extended school day from 8.00am until 6.00pm. Before and After School Club is run by a member of staff known to the children and who offers a range of fun and engaging activities each day in a nurturing environment.
*For pupils from Reception to Year 6. Separate fees apply for Nursery Pupils
Before School Club 8.00am - 8.30am (Reception to Year 6)
Children may arrive at school between 8:00 and 8:10am if parents require an earlier than normal drop off. Reception children should be dropped off at the Nursery and children in Years 1 to 6 are dropped off at the front door of the Prep School.
After School Club (Nursery to Year 6) until 6.00pm
The After School Club consists of afternoon tea and activities until 6.00pm. Provision is based in the Prep Hall. Reception, Year 1 and 2 children are looked after separately in the Nursery, while children in Years 3 to 6 are based in the Prep School.
